# 2 Chronicles Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

**2** The priests could not even enter the LORD's temple because His glory filled it completely.

**3** When all the Israelites saw the fire fall and the glory of the LORD over the temple, they knelt on the pavement with their faces to the ground and worshiped, saying, "He is good! His faithful love endures forever!"

**4** Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.

**5** King Solomon sacrificed 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep and goats. And so the king and all the people dedicated God's temple.

**6** The priests took their positions, and the Levites stood with the LORD's musical instruments that King David had made for praising the LORD — "His faithful love endures forever" — whenever David would lead worship through them. Across from the Levites, the priests blew their trumpets, while all Israel stood.

**7** Solomon consecrated the center of the courtyard in front of the LORD's temple and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings there, because the bronze altar he had made was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and fat portions.

**8** Solomon celebrated the festival for seven days, along with all Israel — an enormous assembly gathered from as far as Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.

**9** On the eighth day they held a closing assembly, having celebrated the altar's dedication for seven days and the festival for seven days.

**10** On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people home. They were joyful and glad because of all the good things the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for His people Israel.

**11** Solomon completed the LORD's temple and the royal palace. Everything he had planned to do in the LORD's temple and his own palace succeeded.

**12** The LORD appeared to Solomon at night and said: "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for Myself as a temple for sacrifices.

**13** When I shut up the heavens so there is no rain, or command locusts to devour the land, or send a plague among My people,

**14** if My people, who are called by My name, will humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

**15** Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

**16** I have now chosen and consecrated this temple so that My name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will always be there.

**17** "As for you, if you walk before Me faithfully as your father David did, obeying everything I commanded you and keeping My decrees and laws,

**18** then I will establish your royal throne, as I promised your father David when I said, 'You will never fail to have a man ruling over Israel.'

**19** "But if you turn away and abandon the decrees and commands I have given you and go off to serve and worship other gods,

**20** then I will uproot Israel from My land, which I gave them, and I will reject this temple I have consecrated for My name. I will make it an object of ridicule among all peoples.

**21** This temple will become a heap of rubble. Everyone who passes by will be appalled and ask, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?'

**22** And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of Egypt, and embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them — that is why He brought all this disaster on them.'"


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **7:1**: Fire from heaven — God answers Solomon's prayer not with words but with fire. This is unmistakable divine approval. The Chronicler adds this detail (absent from Kings) because he wants there to be no doubt: God accepted this temple.

- **7:14**: The most famous verse in 2 Chronicles, and arguably the theological thesis of the entire book. God gives His people a four-step path home: humble yourselves, pray, seek My face, turn from evil. The promise is not just forgiveness but healing — restoration of the land itself.

- **7:21-22**: The Chronicler's audience already knows what happened to the temple. They are living in the aftermath of 7:19-22. Which means 7:14 isn't history for them — it's an invitation.


— PNEUMA
